name: Shape Detection: FaceDetector and TextDetector
plain: Finds faces and printed text in an image (experimental flag only).
meaning: Face boxes and text blocks from images without server calls. Experimental and off by default; not a stable surface.

access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: Finds faces and printed text in an image (experimental flag only).

limits.headline: Can find faces and printed text in a picture, but only with a special setting on
limits.user_action: You turn on a flag in Chrome, then pick or load a picture.
can: Find where faces are in a picture, without naming them
Find where printed text sits in a picture
Work on a photo or a camera frame the page already has
cannot: Work in normal Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari without the flag turned on
Work on Android or iPhone browsers
Work on pictures the page does not have
limits.differs: Only desktop Chrome and Edge with a flag turned on. No phone browsers.

story.what_it_is: A page can find faces and printed words in a picture, but only in a test mode.

marketing.name: Shape Detection API
marketing.pitch: Chrome's docs describe detecting faces, barcodes and text in images, with faces and text still behind a flag.

story.for_you: You will not meet it on normal sites. It is behind a flag, so only people who turn it on see it.
story.for_makers: Makers would use it for photo tags, camera filters and reading text from pictures. It is not on by default because face finding raises privacy worries.

use_cases.example: A photo editor crops a picture around the faces it finds.
A camera filter app places stickers on faces.
A tool reads text on a worksheet photo for a translator.
A page reads out the text in a picture to a blind user.
A bad site could count faces in a photo you upload.
A browser game moves a character as you turn your head.

technical_bounds: No stable release in any browser

history.change: Introduced behind experimental flag; no stable release since
